lines: It found its purpose. I prefer equipment that knows when to stop.
It did the job when fear was loud. That is praise enough.
Good gear earns trust the moment trouble tests it.
The fresh wear along that fastening shows where the strain landed.
This edge took a hard blow and kept together.
Dirt is packed deep into the straps. Clean it before it dries there.
The material nearly failed at this spot. I would reinforce it.
That repair held, but I would not ask it to hold twice.
The new nick near the edge needs a careful pass on the stone.
The buckles stayed closed through the fight. That matters.
I can see exactly where the weight pulled against the stitching.
Repair the damage before trusting this in another battle.
Wear tells the truth about a fight better than the person carrying it.
The straps stretched, but they did not tear.
This came back used hard and maintained poorly.
I would replace the weakest fastening while the rest is still sound.
The edge is recoverable. Give me time at the bench.
A good cleaning will reveal whether any cracks are hiding under the grime.
It protected someone and survived. Now it has earned a repair.
Bring used gear back early. Small damage is easier to mend than broken trust.
Still sharp, still waiting. That is better than needing it twice.
No fresh nicks. That edge never had to answer trouble.
Unused steel is good news when the village stayed safe.
The leather has no new scratches and the straps have not stretched.
Every buckle still sits straight.
The edge is clean because it met no resistance.
Keep it oiled even if it never leaves the rack.
No one drew this weapon. I am glad they did not need to.
The grip shows no sweat, dirt, or impact marks.
Nothing shifted in storage, so the balance is still sound.
Unused gear still needs inspection. Neglect does damage quietly.
The fittings are firm and the binding is dry.
I would store this exactly as it is, within easy reach.
Do not swing it just to prove it works.
A weapon that stays sheathed can still do its job.
The straps are clean enough to show they never carried weight.
No repair is needed. A light coat of oil will be enough.
Preparation is not wasted simply because the raid never came.
Check the rack, keep the edge covered, and leave it ready.
This is what I like to see after a quiet watch.
